note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Self-Contrastive Steering: from the entanglement problem to the method and its results

nodes.name: Conditional embeddings needed
nodes.description: A single universal text embedding cannot satisfy fine-grained needs, so conditional text embeddings that focus on a specified aspect are crucial.

nodes.name: Fine-tuning approaches are costly
nodes.description: Existing conditional-embedding methods (InstructOR, C-STS, InBedder, HyperCL) require large data and high fine-tuning cost and sacrifice the LLM's general capabilities.

nodes.name: Prompt-based extraction
nodes.description: Training-free prompt methods (PromptEOL, PonTE) compress the text (and condition) into the hidden state of the last token via 'in one word' prompts and use it directly as the embedding.

nodes.name: Conditional embeddings stay entangled
nodes.description: Prompt-conditioned embeddings still encode condition-irrelevant general information, e.g. average cosine similarity between general and conditional embeddings is 0.763 on TweetEmotion, which degrades distance measurements.

nodes.name: SCS method
nodes.description: Self-Contrastive Steering (SCS) is a training-free plug-and-play method that derives an unconditional embedding and a conditional embedding from the same prompt-wrapped text and contrasts them to steer the embedding toward condition-related information.

nodes.name: Unconditional embedding via attention mask
nodes.description: The unconditional text embedding is obtained at a chosen layer by modifying the attention mask and positional encoding to mask the condition, costing only one additional multi-head self-attention computation.

nodes.name: Two steering strategies
nodes.description: Direct elimination (DE) subtracts the unconditional value vector from the conditional one, while projection-based elimination (PE) removes only the component of the conditional vector along the unconditional vector; a scaling factor alpha controls the post-intervention norm.

nodes.name: SCS outperforms baselines
nodes.description: With LLaMA3-8B-Instruct, SCS is best in 6 of 7 cases across clustering, STS and triplet alignment datasets and best on average, with gains on all seven datasets, e.g. 6% and 8.2% on the two I.STSB metrics.

nodes.name: DE suffices
nodes.description: The simpler SCS-DE achieves better average performance than PE, indicating projection may be unnecessary.

nodes.name: Comparable to supervised methods
nodes.description: SCS achieves performance comparable to supervised contrastive learning approaches, showing the potential of directly extracting conditional embeddings from LLMs.

nodes.name: Efficient at inference
nodes.description: SCS adds only a small runtime overhead per sample (e.g. about 70ms to 80ms in Table 2).

nodes.name: Generalizes across LLMs
nodes.description: SCS gives consistent gains across LLaMA3-8B, LLaMA3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B and their instruct versions, with larger gains on non-instruction-tuned models due to their weaker instruction following.

nodes.name: Generalizes across prompts and conditions
nodes.description: SCS improves results across six prompts, reduces variance across prompts, and improves across six conditions.

isolated_nodes.name: Intervention position matters
isolated_nodes.description: Intervening at the attention head, FFN output or hidden state all improve performance, with the optimal position dataset-dependent (Table 3).

isolated_nodes.name: Optimal layer varies
isolated_nodes.description: The optimal intervention layer is 3 for TweetEmo, 7 for Amazon-R and 4 for Amazon-C, while layers 5 or 6 generally help all three datasets (Fig 3a).

isolated_nodes.name: Scaling factor sensitivity
isolated_nodes.description: The optimal scaling factor is 15 for TweetEmo, 10 for Amazon-R and 5 for Amazon-C, and values 7, 10 or 12 work well for all three (Fig 3b).

isolated_nodes.name: Improves middle and later layers
isolated_nodes.description: SCS-DE improves PonTE across all middle and later output layers and shifts the optimal layer for conditional embeddings (Fig 3c).

isolated_nodes.name: Limitations
isolated_nodes.description: SCS requires access to LLM internals so it is inapplicable to black-box LLMs, and it was not validated on 70B-scale models.

structural_reasoning: The entanglement problem in prompt-based conditional embeddings motivates SCS; its two-view construction and steering strategies lead to benchmark and generalization results. Hyperparameter analyses and limitations are isolated.
